title: Efficient Maximization of Propagation Closure
summary: A simple greedy heuristic builds good insufficient variable sets, but efficiently maximizing their propagation closure for global pruning remains open.

formal_statement.body: Efficiently find $V$ with $K\subseteq V\subseteq X$, $\operatorname{Propagate}^{*}(V)\ne X$, maximizing $|\operatorname{Propagate}^{*}(V)|$.

scope.domain: Automated symmetric cryptanalysis, specifically global pruning in guess-and-determine attack search.
assumptions: The selected set V must contain K, lie within X, and remain insufficient under propagation.
parameters: K: the currently known variable set
V: the insufficient variable set to be selected
Propagate*: the propagation closure used for pruning
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find an efficient method that selects a feasible V with maximum propagation closure, beyond the reported greedy heuristic.

citations.label: Automatic Search of Attacks on Round-Reduced AES and Applications

progress.summary: The source explicitly says that the problem remains and reports a simple greedy heuristic for building good sets. It highlights a tradeoff between time spent pruning the DAG and time spent exploring it.
citation_labels: Charles Bouillaguet et al., Automatic Search of Attacks on Round-Reduced AES and Applications
